source: Durian Orchard (ការដាំធូរេន), by Vann Thana Busab and Montry Vong Phanith, published by the Northwest Cambodia Provinces Fruit Culture Development Committee (Battambang), 1998, 59pp, AIDOC code 178-001
text:
For a young, not-yet-fruiting durian tree, the source gives a fertilizing schedule keyed to leaf-flush number (the tree produces a new flush of leaves several times a year, and each flush is a natural point to fertilize because the roots are then actively taking up nutrients to support new leaf growth):

Flush 1 through 3: apply about 5kg of well-rotted compost/manure per tree, per flush.

Flush 4: apply about 5kg of compost/manure per tree, plus chemical fertilizer 15-15-15 or 16-16-16 at 150-200 grams per tree (amount should be adjusted upward gradually as the tree grows larger).

For trees that have not yet begun fruiting, an alternative schedule ties fertilizing to season rather than flush number: in the early rainy season, apply chemical fertilizer 15-15-15 or 16-16-16 at about 3g per tree per centimeter of canopy diameter; in the late rainy season, apply well-rotted manure at 15-30kg per tree (roughly 3-10 baskets) plus chemical fertilizer 15-15-15 or 16-16-16 at about 3g per tree per centimeter of canopy diameter.

The source notes that as canopy diameter increases with age, the applied fertilizer amount should scale up in proportion, and fertilizer should be broadcast in a ring under the drip-line of the canopy rather than piled at the trunk.
